notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 12 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingindustri1212cont), the 26 weekly issues from 2 January to 25 June 1912, all Tuesdays. Same method as the later volumes of this source: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers. extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; 45 item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image. No January row passed the placement and selection steps, so the published rows run from 6 February. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image was left out, and a cost past a column break was taken from the OCR text only where the instalments add up to the total. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image (32 of 122): contracts the page already carries in full from the San Francisco Call (9), minor work such as signs, small repairs, a barn and foundation-only permits (9), unit counts or lots that do not fit one parcel of today (5: the two buildings of nine flats on Powell north of Green, two buildings on Oak west of Cole, a corner at Leavenworth and Lombard), storey counts that contradict the roll (4), and small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (5, held for a page). 20 rows on pages that already carry a Call entry of the same fortnight (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery) were trimmed to what this paper adds (the architect, the contractor, the kind of building or the price). Where the price differs from the Call entry the page image read here is given and the Call entry left alone (349 29th Street: $7,620 here, four instalments of $1,905, against $7,020 in the Call entry). At 2152 Union Street the Call entry gives one price of $11,280 for two contracts this paper lists separately ($5,600 and $5,680); the first is published with its contractor. The permit of 21 May for flats at Jones and Vallejo prints J. F. Dunn under the label 'Contractor' beside the contractor proper; he is not recorded, since the label for an architect is not what was printed. One held fact of the later run (16th Avenue north of Lake, a $500 garage alteration of December 1917) sits on a parcel seeded here and stays held as minor work.

coverage.remaining: Unread: the two 1911 half-year volumes on the Internet Archive (vol. 11 pt. 1 and pt. 2). In this volume: 86 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 5 more were held for a page at the image. 949 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
